title: Argo quality control flag scale (Reference table 2)

source.citation: Argo Data Management Team, Argo user's manual, version 3.44.0, July 2025, Section 3.2.1 "Reference table 2: quality control flag scale", page 76

text.made_by: pdftotext 4.00 -raw (default Latin1 encoding) of the PDF above; CRLF line ends

source.quoted_as: each text is the table cell as the extraction prints it, its line breaks joined by one space; nothing else is changed

1.real_time: Good data. All Argo real-time QC tests passed. These measurements are good within the limits of the Argo real-time QC tests.
1.delayed_mode: Good data. No adjustment is needed, or the adjusted value is statistically consistent with good quality reference data. An error estimate is supplied.

2.real_time: Probably good data. These measurements are to be used with caution.
2.delayed_mode: Probably good data. Delayed-mode evaluation is based on insufficient information. An error estimate is supplied.

3.meaning: Probably bad data that are potentially adjustable
3.real_time: Probably bad data. These measurements are not to be used without scientific adjustment, e.g. data affected by sensor drift but may be adjusted in delayed-mode.
3.delayed_mode: Probably bad data. An adjustment may (or may not) have been applied, but the value may still be bad. An error estimate is supplied.

4.real_time: Bad data. These measurements are not to be used. A flag '4' indicates that a relevant real-time qc test has failed. A flag '4' may also be assigned for bad measurements that are known to be not adjustable, e.g. due to sensor failure.
4.delayed_mode: Bad data. Not adjustable. Adjusted data are replaced by FillValue.

8.real_time: Estimated value (interpolated, extrapolated or other estimation).
8.delayed_mode: Estimated value (interpolated, extrapolated or other estimation).

9.real_time: Missing value. Data parameter will record FillValue.
9.delayed_mode: Missing value. Data parameter will record FillValue.
